title: Top K with a heap
short: Keep the k biggest items seen so far in a small heap.
what: To find the k largest items, you don't need to sort everything. Keep a min-heap of size k: the smallest of your current top k sits on top. Each new item that beats the top pushes it out. At the end the heap holds the top k, and its top is the k-th largest.
analogy: A top-3 leaderboard. A new score only gets on the board if it beats the lowest score shown, and that lowest score is the one that drops off.

frames.label: k = 3
frames.say: Keep the 3 biggest of 5 1 9 3 7 2 8. Put the first three in a min-heap. The smallest of them, 1, sits on top.

frames.label: next: 3
frames.say: Push 3. The heap now holds 4 items, one more than k. The heap keeps the smallest on top: still 1.

frames.label: next: 3
frames.say: Pop the top: 1 leaves. Now the heap is the top 3 so far: 3, 5, 9, and 3 is the bar to beat.

frames.label: next: 7
frames.say: 7 comes in and pushes out the smallest, 3. The bar rises to 5.

frames.label: next: 2
frames.say: 2 comes in and is the smallest right away, so it is popped straight back out. The heap doesn't change.

frames.label: done
frames.say: Done. The heap holds the top 3, and its top, 7, is the 3rd largest. Each step costs log k, not log n.

when: The k largest, smallest, closest or most frequent
A stream of data where you can't keep everything
Sorting everything would be wasteful when k is small
watch: For the k largest use a min-heap, not a max-heap: the top is the one to kick out.
heapq is a min-heap only. For a max-heap, push -x and flip the sign back.
To rank by a score, push tuples: (score, item).
